segments.title: Cold Open: Three Wrong Numbers
segments.notes: Blackwell opens the telethon on a laptop that keeps crashing the feed, abandons the video-call room entirely, and reads the hotline out wrong twice before landing on 424-253-6676.

segments.title: The 13 Freak Street Pledge Ladder
segments.notes: Blackwell walks the live Kickstarter page at 19 backers and $2,340, rolls the pre-launch pitch video, and climbs the tier ladder from a $25 special thanks to the $5,000 original sketch.

segments.title: Analog Lines Only: Bill Stern and Bang the Pot
segments.notes: A caller's video link floods the feed with noise and the desk goes phone-only; Bill calls in on potty training, Charles reports sinus surgery, and Blackwell builds a donation-update graphic live before chat adopts a pot and pan as the alert bell.

segments.title: Incentive Escalation
segments.notes: Blackwell floats olive oil foot, thirty eggs in thirty seconds, a chat-voted beard at $5,000 and eyebrow work at $7,000, while Tim recounts his rejected Jimmy Fallon egg auditions and Kendelle sweeps through frame.

segments.title: Crum Reports From the Rented Call Center
segments.notes: Debate analyst Crum joins on a low-latency feed in camouflage headphones, claims a $50,000 call-center rental, and spends the block complaining that Blackwell is not forwarding him any calls.

segments.title: Kendelle Anchors the Phones
segments.notes: Blackwell hands Kendelle the headset and leaves the desk; she fields Bill's call, issues a seven-stage apology procedure, confesses to binocular surveillance of the neighbors, and holds the line until Blackwell returns.

segments.title: Ligotti, Tolstoy, and the Kickstarter Math
segments.notes: Blackwell takes Tim's apology call and Andy Bulldock's Thomas Ligotti report, cites the statistic that pledges split 50-60 percent across the first and last 72 hours, and runs the cast and crew roster including Fiona Nova and Jace Armstrong.

segments.title: Odie, Claire, and Two Fraud Reports
segments.notes: Odie calls in as the group's secret hidden member and confirms he has seen everyone's anatomy; Claire reports a $790 card fraud pulled from her purse at a stand-up show, and Blackwell reveals the Kickstarter's own debit card was compromised before it arrived.

segments.title: The Pants-Shitting Zone
segments.notes: Three Scary Stories to Tell in the Dark readings — The Thing, The Green Ribbon and The Red Spot — split by a call from Simity Sam and capped with a scroll through the site's 2016 comment section.

segments.title: Sushi for a Low-FODMAP Desk
segments.notes: The desk hunts for food Kendelle can actually eat, settles on a Kaiyu Sushi bento, and takes calls on the order while Blackwell promises Tim a baked salmon roll.

segments.title: Chat Votes on the Anchor's Face
segments.notes: The total clears $5,000 and Blackwell opens a Twitch poll on his facial hair; eighty-stash, lightning sideburns, chin strap and the Tobias Beacher split the vote before the Beacher wins.

segments.title: Kendelle Plays GTA 6 While the Anchor Shaves
segments.notes: Blackwell points the camera at Kendelle and leaves to shave; she narrates a midlife-crisis character build, a furniture-moving errand, a prison-girlfriend pickup, and doctor's orders against snacking.

segments.title: The Reveal and the Headshot Campaign
segments.notes: Blackwell returns with patchy lightning sideburns; Claire calls to declare the look proof of untapped facial range and demands professional headshots, Chuck calls to push the $40,000, and Kendall's eyebrow-plucking grievance is aired.

segments.title: Tim Lanthier Drives In; Power Half Hour Playback
segments.notes: Tim calls from a backed-up road, Blackwell leaves for the sushi order, and Tim holds the line to chat with a driving song and a financial-despair pitch until the decade-old Power Half Hour video plays over the anchor's lunch.

segments.title: Evil Blood Money and the Cyber Truck Convoy
segments.notes: Chuck calls to offer donations from corrupt friends, a voicemail lands as fifteen seconds of silence, Blackwell tests a dead zone in his kitchen, and Kendall's on-screen crime spree is covered play-by-play.

segments.title: The Cloud Costume Theory
segments.notes: Tim arrives in studio and refuses to speak until the number moves, then argues SNL lifted his Halloween cloud costume; the desk debates bit theft, GTA NPC dialogue lines, and the sushi and Thai order.

segments.title: The Slythery D, The Big Toe, and the Handlebar
segments.notes: Tim reads The Slythery D, Blackwell reads The Big Toe, the total clears $6,000, and the anchor trims into a handlebar mustache before Tim leaves for his improv show.

segments.title: Sonic Literatica
segments.notes: A punishment is administered to the anchor off-camera, a donation pins the total at $69, and Propaganda calls to request a Mandarin-signed Blu-ray and a censored reading of Sonic fan fiction.

segments.title: Haunted Trousers and The Dream
segments.notes: Bray reports a neighborhood overrun with ducks; a paranormal researcher classifies the glowing disembodied trousers he met on his street as a category-three ecto-beam; Blackwell finishes The Dream and Matt Liddell calls asking for Crum.

segments.title: Crum's Freestyle Thank-You
segments.notes: Crum abandons the call-center bit for a rapid-fire subscriber rap over a control-room beat, and a $500 donation pushes the total past $7,400.

segments.title: Wordle, Bonsai Bullfrog, and the Cat Cameo
segments.notes: A first-time GTA viewer calls for a full explainer, Blackwell recaps the tiers and plays Wordle, Bonsai Bullfrog grills Crum about Munch and the Rock-afire ape, and the cats are coaxed out with churu.

segments.title: Sign-Off and the Freak Street Raid
segments.notes: Blackwell closes at $7,469, sets $10,000 inside 72 hours as the target, pledges to be back the following day with Sunday off, and raids out with a request for project shout-outs.

characters.name: Case Blackwell
characters.notes: Anchored the full six-hour telethon from the living-room couch, working a single phone line, a crashing laptop, and a chat poll on his own face.

characters.name: Kendelle
characters.notes: Swept the set, anchored the phone lines for eleven minutes, and played GTA 6 on camera while Blackwell went off to shave.

characters.name: Crum
characters.notes: Joined remotely from a rented call center in camouflage headphones, received no calls, and closed his shift with a freestyle subscriber rap.

storylines.beat: [06:21:37] Case closed the Freak Street telethon at $7,469 and confirmed he would be back on stream the next day, taking Sunday off.
[06:09:26] Crum answered on air for killing Munch and skinning the Rock-afire ape, arguing that Munch "intentionally became a skeleton" and that chat had voted for his own head to explode.

lore_notes.fact: Case launched the 13 Freak Street Kickstarter: a 13-short horror-comedy anthology from sketch group Cigarette Sandwich, hosted by John Madison, directed by Fiona Nova, produced by Jace Armstrong, with a $40,000 goal and a $5,000 original-sketch tier.
Kendelle's on-air dietary restrictions logged as low-FODMAP, gluten intolerance, and no sesame.
Case debuted the chat-voted Tobias Beacher beard with botched lightning sideburns after the telethon passed $5,000.
Case traded the beard for a handlebar mustache at $6,000, noting it matched his father James's at 40.
Crum declared himself "a new guy" working on himself and stated he cannot return to hell without dying again.
Crum confirmed he is legally obligated to keep accepting money from a political PAC for the next ten years.
Crum confirmed he is suing chat; viewers began organizing a class action against him.

episode_summary: Barely Informed News anchor Case Blackwell hosted a six-hour Freak Street telethon from his living-room couch, working a single phone line to raise $40,000 for Cigarette Sandwich's 13-short horror anthology 13 Freak Street. The broadcast was hobbled by a crashing laptop, two wrong hotline numbers, and a remote call-center appearance by debate analyst Crum, who fielded no calls across four hours of waiting. By sign-off the network had raised $7,469, the anchor had surrendered his beard to a chat poll, and the desk closed on a handlebar mustache.
